title: Oldest living individual trees
measure: Age in years, as of 2026. Single-trunk (non-clonal) trees that are still alive. Where a source gives a range, the lower end is used for ranking, so nothing is overstated. Clonal trees such as Old Tjikko are excluded because their roots, not their trunks, are old.

entries.name: Gran Abuelo (Alerce Milenario)
entries.note: 3,655 years is a ring-counted minimum (incomplete core). The 5,484 figure comes from a 2022 statistical model by climatologist Jonathan Barichivich, who puts an 80% chance on the tree being over 5,000. Other scientists say only a full ring count can settle it.
entries.source: Wikipedia, List of oldest trees (verified minimum); The Guardian (2022), on Barichivich's model

entries.name: Unnamed bristlecone (Schulman tree)
entries.note: Germinated about 3050 BCE according to the Rocky Mountain Tree-Ring Research OldList. Cored by Edmund Schulman, aged by Tom Harlan, but the core is now missing, so the age can't be rechecked.
entries.source: Rocky Mountain Tree-Ring Research OldList, via Wikipedia

entries.name: Methuselah
entries.note: Ring-counted (crossdated) by Edmund Schulman and Tom Harlan in 1957, germination c. 2833 BCE. Another researcher, Matthew Salzer, couldn't reproduce the count because the core is missing and estimates about 4,666, so even this one has a caveat.
entries.source: Rocky Mountain Tree-Ring Research OldList; Wikipedia, Methuselah (pine tree)
